gap: No result ChatGPT got states an independent measurement of any 2026 release. pv magazine USA's Andrew Riha drew 4.87 kWh (97% of the rated 5,024 Wh) from the Anker SOLIX S5000 and measured about 10 W of idle drain. The Solar Lab measured the BLUETTI Apex 200 at 90% efficiency and 12.8 W idle. The same lab's figures for the older models it is weighed against are lower: F3800 Plus 84%, DELTA 3 Ultra 82% with about 22 W idle. The DELTA 3000 Gen4 and TITAN 5000 have no independent test yet.
standout_why: I compared against the cited pages homepowerfacts.com/new-power-stations, energysage.com/solar-generators-overview and us.best-batteries.com/product-launches, the uncited GearJunkie best-portable-power-stations page, and the PR Newswire Apex 200 release (a press release with maker claims only). homepowerfacts says it does no hands-on testing and gives only maker and press figures. EnergySage says 'EnergySage did not test these models for this update', and it covers none of the 2026 releases. best-batteries lists launches with vendor claims only. GearJunkie covers none of the 2026 releases and gives no measured usable capacity for any model. ChatGPT's answer itself said 'The newest models have limited independent long-term testing.' stationarena.com/new-releases could not be opened (certificate error), so it was not checked. Popular Mechanics (uncited) blocked fetching.
decides: The measurements back the new S5000 over the older F3800 Plus on usable energy: about 4.87 kWh measured, against 3,840 Wh rated at 84% measured efficiency, which is roughly 3.2 kWh. The F3800 Plus still has more output (6,000 W against 4,500 W). The measurements also support the Apex 200 over the DELTA 3 Ultra as an efficient mid-size choice: 90% against 82% efficiency, and 12.8 W against about 22 W idle, both from the same lab. Against the Elite 200 V2, StorageReview measured 1.91 kWh delivered (92% of rated). The Apex 200's gain over it is solar input and expansion, not measured efficiency. The DELTA 3000 Gen4 and TITAN 5000 have no independent test, so 'wait for tests' remains the honest advice for those two.

findings.label: Usable energy delivered on a full discharge
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S5000 deep-dive review: 5 kWh on wheels, tested through a real power outage (Andrew Riha, pv magazine USA, 2026-10-28; Now.Solar repost)
findings.note: 120 V outlets, pre-release unit, Northern California. The author says the figure is the app's reading, not a metered output. 4.87 / 5.024 = 96.9%. 240 V output was not tested. Original article: https://pv-magazine-usa.com/2026/10/28/anker-solix-s5000-deep-dive-review-5-kwh-on-wheels-tested-through-a-real-power-outage/

findings.label: Round-trip efficiency
findings.value: 78% (6.24 kWh drawn from the wall for a full charge)
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S5000 deep-dive review (Andrew Riha, pv magazine USA, 2026-10-28)
findings.note: AC charge at the 1,800 W setting. 4.87 / 6.24 = 78%. Each 1% of displayed charge took 61–62 Wh from the wall.

findings.label: Idle drain with AC output on and no load
findings.value: about 10 W (5% of charge lost in 24 h); about 7 W from the wall when plugged in and full
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S5000 deep-dive review (Andrew Riha, pv magazine USA, 2026-10-28)
findings.note: Anker's own figure is 8.8 W. The author puts the 7 W plugged-in draw at about 60 kWh a year.

findings.label: AC charge power at the 1,800 W setting
findings.value: about 1.79 kW for 2 h 49 min, then about 1.43 kW for the last 50 min (about 1.7 kW average)
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S5000 deep-dive review (Andrew Riha, pv magazine USA, 2026-10-28)
findings.note: 120 V wall charge, about 3 h 39 min in total. At the 1,000 W setting the charge took 65% longer and used 1.7% less wall energy.

findings.label: Real outage runtime
findings.value: 61.5 h on a large refrigerator plus phones and small devices, from 100% to 18%
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S5000 deep-dive review (Andrew Riha, pv magazine USA, 2026-10-28)
findings.note: PG&E Public Safety Power Shutoff. The author estimates about 4 kWh used, an average load of about 65 W. The load was not lab-controlled.

findings.label: Fridge runtime and 120 V recharge time
findings.value: about 86 h on a refrigerator; about 3.5 h empty to full on a 120 V outlet
findings.source_title: I Tested Anker's New SOLIX S5000, and It Ran My Fridge for Days (Paul Rankin, BobVila.com, 2026-10-28)
findings.note: Florida home, about a month of use. Fridge run to depletion under normal operation; the fridge's draw was not reported. Anker's 99-minute claim needs 240 V, which was not tested.

findings.label: Efficiency and idle draw
findings.value: 90% efficiency; 12.8 W idle with the inverter on and no AC load
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Apex 200 Review: A Powerful and Smart Expandable Power Station (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The page does not explain how efficiency was computed, and gives no author or date. The Solar Lab works out that 12.8 W idle would empty the battery in about 8.3 days.

findings.label: AC charge time from a standard wall outlet
findings.value: about 2 h 21 min to full, pulling 1,800 W
findings.note: The lab also reports reaching the full 3,000 W solar input with both inputs in use, but gives no separate wattage reading.

findings.label: Observed solar input with a BLUETTI SORA 500 array
findings.value: 270 W peak for an hour, about 190 W average; about 50% charged in 6 h of sun
findings.source_title: Bluetti Apex 200 Power Station Review (TJ Donegan, Reviewed, 2026-11-05)
findings.note: October in New England, about two weeks of use. The article measured no usable capacity, efficiency or idle draw; its 10.5 W standby and 50 dB figures are specs.

findings.label: Energy delivered and energy to recharge
findings.value: 1.91 kWh delivered (92% of 2,073.6 Wh rated); 2.44 kWh from the wall to recharge
findings.source_title: Portable Power Meets Lab-Grade Reliability: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review (Dylan Dougherty, StorageReview, 2025-04-25)
findings.note: Load and method are not stated. 1.91 / 2.0736 = 92.1%. 1.91 / 2.44 = 78% round trip (my arithmetic, not the reviewer's). This is the older model ChatGPT set against the Apex 200.

findings.label: Measured efficiency
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus (The Solar Lab, reviewers Cody & Robbie)
findings.note: Measured by running the 6,000 W inverter from a full battery; no test date given. 3,840 Wh × 0.84 ≈ 3,226 Wh, against the S5000's measured 4.87 kWh. This is the older model ChatGPT set against the S5000.

findings.label: Efficiency, idle draw and AC charge time
findings.value: about 82% efficiency; about 22 W idle with the inverter on; 2 h from 0 to 100% on a household plug
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra Review: A Solid Performer at a Reasonable Price (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The page writes 'watts per hour' but means about 22 W of continuous draw. No author or date is shown. This is the older model ChatGPT set against the DELTA 3000 Gen4. 3,072 Wh × 0.82 ≈ 2,519 Wh.

unsourced: A measured usable capacity or efficiency for the EcoFlow TITAN 5000 / 5000 Plus: searches turned up only launch coverage and spec comparisons, and one comparison site says no independent review had been published as of 2026-11-01.
A measured figure for the EcoFlow DELTA 3000 Gen4: no hands-on or lab review found; per search results it ships late November or early December.
A measured figure for the Jackery Explorer 2000 Plus v2: it is sold only in the UK and EU so far. The measured figures found were for the 2000 v2 and the original 2000 Plus, a different model.
A measured usable capacity (Wh) for the BLUETTI Apex 200: neither The Solar Lab nor Reviewed published one.
A measured usable capacity or idle draw for the F3800 Plus from a named tester: zelpio.com reports 83% of rated and 112 W idle, but names no author or tester, so it is left out.
Measured noise (dB) for any 2026 release: pv magazine says it did not measure noise, and Reviewed and Bob Vila give no dB reading.
stationarena.com/new-releases (a cited rival) could not be opened because of a certificate error, so its content was not checked for measurements.
